title.narrative: Building the Future RJ: Partnership for Sustainable Urban Development with the State Secretariat for Cities

description.narrative:
This proposal presents a set of actions to support the Government of the State of Rio de Janeiro, through the State Secretariat for Cities (SECID), in drive urban projects that prioritize sustainability and inclusivity and are in alignment with national priorities, while Rio de Janeiro’s local and state representatives are better equipped to implement the global agendas for sustainable urban development.
The initiative aligns with the Memorandum of Understanding signed in March 2022 and the Contribution Agreement signed in September 2023 between the Government of the State of Rio de Janeiro and UN-Habitat. Which aims to strengthen urban resilience in the State of Rio de Janeiro, based on the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and the principles of the New Urban Agenda (NAU).
It envisions the following two outcomes, with the State Secretariat for Cities playing a pivotal role in guiding and reviewing project activities and outputs, complementing the technical work from UN-Habitat:
Outcome 1: Strengthened Representation of Rio de Janeiro in National Urban Policy Discussions - Output 1.1: State Cities Conference held - Output 1.2: Training sessions with municipal representatives for the National Cities Conference aligned with the SDGs conducted
Outcome 2: Enhanced capacities of SECID to integrate sustainability in urban development projects - Output 2.1: Impact assessment of priority projects and local scale instruments undertaken in 22 municipalities guided by the 2030 Agenda. - Output 2.2: Guide for Impact Assessment of Public Works Based on Sustainability Criteria developed - Output 2.3: Training sessions for government representatives to use the Impact Assessment Guide conducted
By holding the State Cities Conference (Output 1.1), with the reactivation of the state council, and conducting training sessions aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for municipal representatives (Output 1.2), the project will empower local authorities to contribute effectively to national urban policy discussions. This capacity building will provide them with the knowledge and skills required to participate meaningfully in the knowledge exchange on urban policies at different levels of development, from a perspective that prioritizes sustainable and inclusive urban development, and particular to fully take advantage of the 6th National Cities Conference on November 2024, following the conference central theme: "Cities for All: The Challenge of Integration and Sustainability".
Moreover, the project will enhance the integration of sustainability principles in urban development projects undertaken by the State Secretariat for Cities (SECID). Through undertaking impact assessments of priority projects and local-scale instruments in 22 municipalities (Output 2.1), developing a Guide for Impact Assessment of Public Works (Output 2.2) and conducting training sessions for government representatives to effectively utilize the Impact Assessment Guide (Output 2.3), the project will equip local authorities with the tools and expertise necessary to incorporate sustainability considerations into their urban development initiatives, aligning them with the SDGs and the broader goals of improving quality of life and reducing inequalities.
